basis: Cerebellar and spinal cord degeneration or abnormal development define this neurologic umbrella; other organ disease varies by subtype.
External/middle ear malformations and hearing loss define disease; hypogonadism and global developmental delay each occur in 30-79%.
Disordered plasmalogen biosynthesis with uncontrolled ether-lipid synthesis and a defining neurologic phenotype.
Bacterial infection umbrella encompassing different sites; pulmonary or neurologic damage is not established across most patients.
MHC class I immunodeficiency; glomerulonephritis directly damages kidneys and is reported in 1/1 patients, with substantial small-sample uncertainty.
Avulavirus infection; human conjunctivitis is typically transient and does not establish lasting ocular damage.
Malignancy usually originates in deep extremity soft tissues; supplied HPO reports subcutaneous tumor nodules in 80-99%, supporting subcutis occupation.
Gracile bones and limb/thoracic hypoplasia establish skeletal disease; pulmonary and adrenal hypoplasia lack frequencies establishing common involvement.
SEC63-associated polycystic liver disease is supported by parent and hepatic cyst phenotypes; isolated kidney wording in the definition conflicts with these.
Reported syndrome includes skeletal and skin abnormalities beyond the placental lesion; respiratory insufficiency and intracranial hemorrhage lack frequencies.
Rickettsia japonica infection; acute rash, eschar and lymphadenopathy do not establish additional lasting organ damage.
Nephronophthisis causes renal tubulointerstitial degeneration; the peptide-metabolism ancestor alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Benign adipose neoplasm originates in the colon; its tissue composition does not imply skin involvement.
Named metabolic enzyme deficiency; no supplied clinical phenotype establishes damage to another organ.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; muscular, cerebral and retinal abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
AML/MDS and colorectal adenomatous polyposis are defining manifestations; uveal melanoma occurs in 2/8 (<30%); other tumor risks do not qualify.
Thiamine deficiency defines the metabolic disorder; peripheral neuropathy and cardiac dysfunction define its dry and wet clinical forms.
Oocyte/embryo maturation failure and female infertility affect reproductive function without an endocrine or other covered organ disorder.
Blepharophimosis and intellectual disability define the syndrome group; eyelids are ocular and intellectual disability is neurologic.
Site-unspecified neoplastic polyp; gastrointestinal assignment reflects the usual adenomatous polyp setting, but no anatomical site is supplied.
Microcephaly, cortical malformations and skeletal growth abnormalities define syndrome; patent ductus arteriosus occurs in 2/4 (50%).
Monoamine metabolism disorder with defining cognitive impairment/intellectual disability; behavioral features do not make it purely psychiatric.
ABCB1-associated inflammatory bowel disease directly inflames intestinal tissue and is immune-mediated.
Neurologic pain disorder involving peripheral nerve distributions; no additional organ damage is inherent.
Inherited lichen planus is immune-mediated cutaneous disease; damaging oral involvement in at least 30% of this familial subtype is not established.
